TL;DR: the hour before bed matters more than total screen time. In a 2025 study of 1,200 kids aged 6 to 9, screens in the last 60 minutes before lights-out delayed sleep by about 19 minutes, mostly from light, stimulating games or video, and displacement of wind-down routines. The fix is a fixed screens-off time an hour before bed (weekends too), devices charged outside the bedroom, TV in a shared room, and reading in the last half hour, which normalised sleep within about two weeks.
Action: Nothing else needed unless you want a one-line reply drafted for Hannah in the group chat.

In Canada, EFT (electronic funds transfer) is the broad term for moving money electronically, such as direct deposits and pre-authorized debits. ACH is the US system name; the Canadian counterpart is Payments Canada's clearing system, which is why people on the call often use them interchangeably. Wire transfers and Interac e-Transfer are separate rails.
Action: Draft a two-line explainer you can drop into a doc if that's useful.

A common rule of thumb: a retention curve has flattened when the period-over-period drop falls to roughly a point or two, and stays there for several consecutive periods, leaving a plateau above zero. The right threshold depends on the cohort size and the period length, so it's worth agreeing it with your team.
Action: Apply this to your cohort data if you share the sheet.
